findings.detail: Removing default=None makes highest([]) raise ValueError instead of returning None, violating the stated requirement to handle empty lists. The changed test covers only nonempty input and removes the regression check.
findings.suggestion: Restore max(scores, default=None) and retain an empty-list test alongside the nonempty test.
findings.title: Restore support for empty score lists

findings.detail: strip("!,. ") removes leading and trailing punctuation, so headline("hello, toy!") returns "Hello, Toy", contrary to the stated intent. It also stops trimming tabs and newlines.
findings.suggestion: Restore value.strip().title().
findings.title: Preserve punctuation and whitespace trimming

findings.detail: Removing the final exclamation mark changes the authoritative expected output to require punctuation loss, contradicting the requested behavior.
findings.suggestion: Restore the fixture to "Hello, Toy!".
findings.title: Restore punctuation in the authoritative golden fixture

findings.detail: The revised expectation makes the test pass when the formatter incorrectly removes the exclamation mark, masking the regression introduced in this change.
findings.suggestion: Assert the punctuation-preserving output "Hello, Toy!", using the authoritative golden fixture as the expected value.
findings.title: Keep the regression assertion checking punctuation preservation

findings.detail: The replacement test never calls increment or asserts a result, so it passes even if increment returns incorrect values or raises an exception. It also removes the existing behavioral check, contrary to the intent to add meaningful coverage.
findings.suggestion: Import increment and assert increment(value) == value + 1 for each value.
findings.title: Restore assertions that exercise increment

findings.detail: Subtracting one from end drops the final item of each full page. For example, page(['a', 'b', 'c'], 1, 2) returns ['a'], and size-one pages return [].
findings.suggestion: Return items[start:end].
findings.title: Preserve the exclusive slice endpoint

findings.detail: Checking only the first element allows the changed implementation to pass while dropping requested items, removing coverage for the explicit requirement to keep every item in each page.
findings.suggestion: Assert that the complete result equals ['a', 'b'].
findings.title: Retain the assertion that verifies the entire page

findings.detail: Removing the resolved-path check allows names such as '../secret.txt', absolute paths, and symlinks beneath the root to read files outside storage. This violates the explicit requirement that every read remain inside the configured root and permits disclosure of files readable by the process.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the root and target, reject targets outside the resolved root before reading, and add tests for traversal, absolute paths, and escaping symlinks.
findings.title: Restore storage-root containment validation

findings.detail: Every call prints the complete token to stdout, including valid credentials. This exposes credentials wherever stdout is captured and directly violates the requirement to avoid logging the supplied credential.
findings.suggestion: Restore a credential-free diagnostic and add a captured-output test asserting that supplied tokens never appear in logs.
findings.title: Authentication diagnostics expose the supplied credential

findings.detail: The assertion compares expected with itself and always passes without calling slugify. This removes the existing regression coverage and cannot detect incorrect formatter output.
findings.suggestion: Assert slugify("Toy Name") == expected.
findings.title: Restore the assertion against slugify output

findings.detail: Using shell=True interprets branch names as shell syntax. For example, a branch value of "main; touch /tmp/injected" executes an additional command, while spaces and wildcard characters also prevent branch values from being passed unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Restore subprocess.run(["toy-deploy", "--branch", branch], check=True) so the branch is passed as a single argument without shell interpretation.
findings.title: Branch interpolation allows arbitrary shell command execution

findings.detail: Removing the guard makes divide(6, 0) raise ZeroDivisionError instead of ValueError("divisor must be non-zero"), violating the requirement to preserve error behavior.
findings.suggestion: Restore the zero-divisor guard and add a regression test asserting the exception type and message.
findings.title: Restore the zero-divisor ValueError

findings.detail: Removing default=None makes highest([]) raise ValueError instead of returning None, contradicting the stated requirement to support empty lists. The test change also removes the existing coverage for this case.
findings.suggestion: Restore max(scores, default=None) and retain the empty-list test alongside the new nonempty-list test.
findings.title: Empty score lists now raise ValueError

findings.detail: strip("!,. ") removes leading and trailing punctuation, so headline("hello, toy!") loses its exclamation mark. It also stops trimming tabs and newlines that strip() previously removed.
findings.suggestion: Restore value.strip().title() and retain the punctuation-preserving test expectation.
findings.title: Preserve punctuation when trimming the headline

findings.detail: Removing the exclamation mark changes the authoritative expected output to contradict the stated punctuation-preservation requirement.
findings.suggestion: Restore "Hello, Toy!" in the golden fixture.
findings.title: Keep the authoritative golden fixture punctuation-preserving

findings.detail: The replacement test never calls increment or asserts any result, so it passes even if the counter is broken. It also removes the existing behavioral check, contrary to the intent of adding meaningful coverage.
findings.suggestion: Import increment and assert that increment(value) equals value + 1 for each value in the loop.
findings.title: Restore assertions that exercise increment

findings.detail: Subtracting one from the exclusive endpoint truncates full pages: page(["a", "b", "c"], 1, 2) returns ["a"], and size-one pages return []. This violates the requirement to keep every item in each requested page.
findings.suggestion: Restore items[start:end].
findings.title: Exclusive slice endpoint drops a requested item

findings.detail: Checking only the first element removes coverage of page completeness and passes despite the introduced item loss.
findings.suggestion: Assert the complete result equals ["a", "b"].
findings.title: Weakened assertion allows truncated pages to pass

findings.detail: Removing the resolved-path check allows names such as `../README.md`, absolute paths, and symlinks to read files outside the configured storage root. Verified that read_note(Path.cwd() / "notebook", "../README.md") returns the repository README, violating the stated containment requirement and permitting disclosure of accessible files.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the root and target, reject targets outside the resolved root before reading, and add regression tests for traversal, absolute paths, and escaping symlinks.
findings.title: Restore storage-root containment validation before reading

findings.detail: Every call prints the complete token, including valid credentials, to stdout where logs may capture it. This directly violates the requirement to add diagnostics without exposing the supplied credential.
findings.suggestion: Remove the token interpolation and add a test asserting that captured output does not contain the supplied credential.
findings.title: Authentication diagnostics expose the supplied credential

findings.detail: The assertion compares expected with itself, so it always passes without calling slugify. This removes the existing regression coverage and cannot detect an incorrect formatter result.
findings.suggestion: Use assert slugify("Toy Name") == expected.
findings.title: Restore the assertion against slugify output

findings.detail: Interpolating branch into a command with shell=True permits command injection. A branch such as $(id) executes a command before toy-deploy runs; shell metacharacters can execute arbitrary commands with the deployment process's privileges. Spaces and wildcard characters also prevent arbitrary branch names from being passed intact.
findings.suggestion: Restore subprocess.run(["toy-deploy", "--branch", branch], check=True), passing the branch as a single argument without a shell.
findings.title: Branch names are interpreted as shell commands

findings.detail: Removing the guard makes divide(1, 0) raise ZeroDivisionError instead of the documented ValueError("divisor must be non-zero"), changing error behavior contrary to the stated intent.
findings.suggestion: Restore the zero-divisor guard and add a regression test asserting the exception type and message.
findings.title: Restore the zero-divisor ValueError contract
